slo_title: Describe the access matrix model for protection

mcq.q: In access lists for objects, an entry consists of:
Which of the following is not a method to implement an access matrix?
Which implementation method uses a set of ordered triples <domain, object, rights-set>?
In capability lists, the capability represents:

options.A: Only the name of the object
options.B: Physical name or address of the object

mcq.answer_text: Physical name or address of the object

mcq.q: Which is a drawback of using a global table for access matrix implementation?

options.B: It is difficult to manage grouping of objects/domains
options.C: It does not require virtual memory
options.D: It is faster than other methods

mcq.answer_text: It is difficult to manage grouping of objects/domains

answer: It is a list for a domain containing objects with their allowed operations, where possession of capability grants access.

sq.q: What is a global table in access matrix implementation?
answer: A global table stores ordered triples <domain, object, rights-set> for all access rights, searched each time an operation is executed.

lq.q: Explain any three methods for implementing an access matrix with their advantages or drawbacks.
answer: Global Table: Uses ordered triples <domain, object, rights-set>; easy to implement but inefficient due to size and I/O needs.
Global Table: Uses ordered triples <domain, object, rights-set>; easy to implement but inefficient due to size and I/O needs.
Access Lists for Objects: Stores access lists per object, efficient in sparse matrices but requires default rights checking.
Access Lists for Objects: Stores access lists per object, efficient in sparse matrices but requires default rights checking.
Capability Lists for Domains: Associates domains with object-capability pairs; direct access control but requires secure management to prevent unauthorized capability use.
